div.head: VI As 1.4
div.ab: ⁊ se ðe þyfðe oft ǽr forworht wære openlice ⁊ to órdale gá ⁊ þar fúl weorðe, þæt hine man slea, butan þa magas oððe se hlaford hine útniman willan be his were ⁊ be fullan ceapgilde ⁊ eac hine on borh gehabban syððan þæt he ælces yfeles geswice. Gif he eft ofer þæt stalie, agifan þa mágas þonne hine swa gewyld swa hine ær út æt þam ordale namon, þam gerefan þe þar togebyrige, ⁊ slea man hine on þa þeofwráce. Gif hine þonne hwa forene forstande ⁊ hine geniman wille, ⁊ he wære fúl æt þam ordale, þæt hine man lecgan ne moste, þæt he wære his feores scyldig, buton he cyng gesohte, ⁊ he him his féorh forgifan wolde, eall swa hit ær æt Gréatanléa ⁊ æt Exanceastre ⁊ æt Þunresfelda gecweden wæs.

And he who has been frequently and publicly convicted of theft, and who goes to the ordeal and is there proved guilty, shall be slain, unless his kinsmen or his lord will ransom him by the payment of his wergeld and the full value of the [stolen] goods; and, in addition, stand surety for him henceforth, that he will desist from every form of crime. If he steals again after this, his kinsmen shall give him back to the reeve to whose jurisdiction the case belongs, in as helpless a condition as he was when they delivered him from the ordeal; and he shall be slain in accordance with the punishment for theft. Futhermore, if anyone stands up for him and wishes to rescue him in order to prevent his being killed, after he has been convicted at the ordeal, he shall forfeit his life unless he appeals to the king, and the king is willing to grant him his life, just as was declared at Grately, and at Exeter, and at Thundersfield.

Et fur qui seps forisfactus fuerit aperte et ad ordalium eat (uadat) et reus appareat, occidatur nisi cognatio eius (tribus sua) uel dominus redimere uelit eum secundum weram suam et pleno ceapgildo et etiam in plegium habere deincips, quod ab omni malo cesset (plegiare, quod semper in reliquum cesset a malo). Et si postea furetur, reddat eum cognacio illa iusticiabilem, sicut ante ab ordalio ceperit, preposito, qui ad hoc pertinebit, et occidatur. Si quis obstabit et eum cripere uelit, reum in ordalio, quin occidatur, uitę suę in culpa sit, nisi regem requirat, et ei uitam perdonare uelit (perdonauerit), sicut apud Greatteleiam et Exoniam et apud Þunresfeldam dictum est
